summary: The passage describes a causal chain originating from persistent Treasury yield curve inversion, which suppresses regional bank net interest margins and induces tightening of commercial and industrial lending standards. This tightening manifests through higher collateral requirements and reduced credit lines, leading to a sharp deceleration in credit growth to SMEs (1.2% y-o-y). The resulting deleveraging transmits contractionary pressure to corporate capital expenditure, causing private fixed investment to fall 0.8% in real terms. Simultaneously, deteriorating earnings revisions and slowing revenue growth drive up default risk premia, widening the investment-grade to high-yield spread by 140 basis points, which further tightens financial conditions for leveraged borrowers dependent on refinancing. The DAG captures two parallel but reinforcing contractionary channels: one through bank lending conditions affecting real investment, and another through credit market pricing affecting financial conditions.
